name: #BlackTechFutures Research Institute
description: Builds national network of HBCUs, city-based researchers, and community institutions focused on local Black tech ecosystems and tech talent. Received PIT Fund support to bolster Black civic tech workforce pipeline.
funding_detail: Public Interest Tech Fund ($250K grant) + philanthropic

name: Abundance New York
description: NYC-focused abundance advocacy organization pushing for housing supply expansion, zoning reform, and permitting streamlining at the city and state level.
funding_detail: Individual donors + paid subscribers; affiliated 501(c)(4) and 501(c)(3) entities

name: Alliance of Civic Technologists (ACT)
description: National umbrella connecting 18+ volunteer civic tech groups. Organizes CityCamp unconferences and Civic Spark convenings. 500+ Discord members.

name: Civic Tech Field Guide
description: World's largest collection of civic tech projects and organizations. Field Guide Friday newsletter (4,300+ subscribers). Open resource cataloguing the global civic tech ecosystem. Key discovery tool for technologists entering the field.

name: Demand Progress
description: Progressive advocacy org with dedicated congressional modernization portfolio. Advocates for transparency, open data, and strengthening legislative branch capacity. Co-authored bipartisan House rules reform proposals with Lincoln Network. Tracks legislative data and capacity issues.

name: Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF)
description: Leading nonprofit defending civil liberties in the digital world through litigation, policy advocacy, and technology development. Shapes government surveillance law, AI policy, and digital rights frameworks.
funding_detail: Individual members; Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Open Society Foundations

name: Federation of American Scientists (FAS)
description: Nonpartisan think tank running Day One Project for policy entrepreneurship. Innovation Ecosystem Job Board for displaced federal technologists (2025). Senior Fellows program.
funding_detail: Schmidt Futures, Open Philanthropy, broad base

name: Inclusive Abundance
description: Coalition of center-left and center-right organizations advancing the abundance agenda: housing supply, energy permitting, regulatory reform, and state capacity. Members include FAS, Niskanen Center, R Street, and New America.

name: Institute for Responsive Government (IRG)
description: Designs practical policy solutions for government service delivery and election administration. Primary focus: automatic voter registration, data sharing between agencies, UX reform for government services (DMVs, tax departments, benefits offices), and online government interfaces. Fiscally sponsored by New Venture Fund (501(c)(3)); separate 501(c)(4) action arm (Responsive Gov Action) conducts issue advocacy. Research outputs targeted directly at state legislators and local administrators. Operates at intersection of service design and democratic infrastructure.
funding_detail: New Venture Fund fiscal sponsorship; philanthropic grants

name: National Conference on Citizenship (NCoC) / Project Redesign
description: Civic health research. Project Redesign focuses on redesigning public services. Co-created TELI program.

name: New Practice Lab
description: New America initiative working to improve government program design for families through policy advocacy and implementation sprints with government agencies.

name: Open New York
description: NYC-based advocacy organization pushing for housing supply expansion through zoning reform and land use deregulation. Primary policy focus is increasing housing production in New York City.

name: Open The Government
description: Coalition advocating for government transparency, open data, and accountability. Works on FOIA reform, open data policy, and government information access. Part of broader good-government advocacy ecosystem.

name: Partnership for Public Service
description: Nonpartisan advocacy and capacity building organization dedicated to better government and stronger democracy. Engages the public about the value of government and public servants; develops and advocates for reform as part of its Government for a New Era initiative; and offers training and development to public servants at the federal, state, and local levels.
funding_detail: Broad philanthropic base; earned revenue from training

name: POPVOX Foundation
description: Congressional modernization nonprofit focused on AI-ready legislatures and legislative branch capacity. Key 2025 wins: secured 4M House Modernization Initiatives Account; advanced CaseCompass unified casework data schema; launched Digital Parliaments Project globally. Runs Future-Proofing Congress newsletter, Casework Navigator, and Keeping Pace AI briefing for Congressional staff.
funding_detail: Hewlett Foundation, Democracy Fund, philanthropic grants

name: Public Interest Technology University Network (PIT-UN)
description: Network of 63 universities co-convened by New America, Ford Foundation, and Hewlett Foundation. $16M+ deployed to 154 projects building the PIT field through curriculum, faculty research, and experiential learning.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Mastercard, McGovern, Raikes, Schmidt Futures, Siegel

name: Recoding America Fund
description: $120M 6-year pooled philanthropic initiative grantmaking for government workforce, digital infrastructure, and procedural reform. Chaired by Jennifer Pahlka.
funding_detail: Pooled fund; inaugural donors not yet fully public

name: Results for America
description: Helps government use evidence and data. Runs What Works Cities and States certifications promoting performance management and evidence-based policymaking.

name: Tech Talent Project
description: Connects senior technologists with government roles and helps administrations build tech leadership capacity from day one. Provides playbooks for state administrations entering first 100 days. Co-runs TELI executive training with Aspen Policy Academy. Has matched technical leaders with state and local government since 2017.

name: Work for America
description: Advocacy organization working to modernize government hiring and talent pipelines, combining direct workforce programs with HR policy advocacy.

name: Apolitical
description: Global social learning network for public servants. 500,000+ members across 170 countries including 50,000+ US civil servants. Offers online courses co-developed with Oxford, LSE, and Georgetown on digital government, AI, climate, and 21st century governance. Launched Government AI Campus in 2023 with 10,000+ enrolled. Co-designed and funded by governments including the UK Cabinet Service. Approved supplier on multiple government learning procurement frameworks.
funding_detail: Government contracts (UK, US, and other governments); subscription fees

name: Aspen Policy Academy (fmr. Aspen Tech Policy Hub)
description: S&T Policy Training (3-week intensive), TELI exec program (5-week, 150+ alumni), Primer, and short courses training STEM professionals on policy impact.
funding_detail: Craig Newmark Philanthropies, Ford Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: Center for Civic Futures (CCF) / AI Readiness Project
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit running the AI Readiness Project. Convenes State Chief AI Officer Community of Practice (30+ states, expanding to 50). Government AI Knowledge Hub launching 2026. Structured pilots for responsible AI in public service.
funding_detail: Rockefeller Foundation ($500K+ for AI Readiness); philanthropic grants

name: Civic Tech Institute (Equitech Futures)
description: 10-week fully funded cohort program training early-career professionals in data science, AI, and civic innovation. Certificate + 1-year alumni mentorship.

name: Decoded Futures (Tech:NYC Foundation)
description: AI capacity-building for NYC nonprofits delivering public services. Cohort-based AI training, industry tech mentors, prototyping support, and grants ($5K-$100K/org).
funding_detail: Robin Hood, Google.org, Salesforce, OpenAI, Altman Foundation, AWS

name: InnovateUS
description: Free digital and AI skills training for public servants at all levels. 200,000+ learners trained across 50 states and 80 countries. 100+ agency partners including NY, MA, PA, GA, OR, and DC. Google.org awarded 5M grant (2025) to expand to 100,000+ additional state and local government workers. Founded by Beth Simone Noveck at Northeastern University Burnes Center.
funding_detail: Google.org (5M grant 2025); Hewlett Foundation; philanthropic grants

name: National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA)
description: Congressionally chartered. Convenes expert panels studying federal agency management, organizational design, and institutional effectiveness.

name: Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP): AI Expo / Talent Initiatives
description: Eric Schmidt-founded initiative (2022) focused on maintaining U.S. technological competitiveness in AI and advanced technology vis-a-vis strategic competitors. Produces policy recommendations, convenes government and industry leaders, and hosts the annual AI Expo for National Competitiveness in DC. Not a fellowship program - included for its role in shaping AI talent policy and government-technology workforce discussions.

name: BetaNYC
description: NYC's civic tech, open data, and open government community (est. 2013). Co-hosts NYC Open Data Week and NYC School of Data (600+ attendees). Builds tools like Boundaries Map. Partners with NYC Office of Technology & Innovation. ACT founding member.
funding_detail: Small grants; NYC OTI partnership; volunteer-driven

name: Chi Hack Night
description: Chicago's weekly civic tech meetup (est. 2012). In-person and online hack nights featuring speakers from government, nonprofits, and tech. Spawned projects like mRelief (food stamps access). Elected board; ACT founding member.

name: Civic Tech Atlanta
description: Atlanta civic tech group hosting monthly hack nights. Provides data support to community organizations (e.g., Sanctuary Food Pantry). Active project lifecycle pipeline. ACT founding member.

name: Civic Tech DC
description: Washington DC volunteer civic hacking group. Hosted Civic Hack DC 2025 (80 participants) focused on open-source tools for Regulations.gov public comment analysis. ACT member.

name: Code for Boston
description: Boston-area civic innovation group. Semi-weekly hybrid hack nights at Cambridge Innovation Center. Building MAPLE (Massachusetts Platform for Legislative Engagement) enabling residents to submit legislative testimony. ACT founding member.

name: Code for BTV
description: Burlington, VT civic tech group hosting biweekly 'Action Nights' (fmr. Hack Night). ACT founding member.

name: Code for Charlottesville
description: Charlottesville, VA civic tech group working with local nonprofits and government agencies on pro bono tech projects. Active GitHub presence through 2025 (Virginia Schools AI policy analysis, native plants DB, Meals on Wheels portal). UVA and PVCC student involvement. ACT member.

name: Code for Dayton
description: Dayton civic tech group with monthly meetings. Projects include Florence Nightingale Museum website and demolition permit monitoring for Preservation Dayton. ACT founding member.

name: Code for Philly
description: Philadelphia civic tech community. Building Clean & Green Philly (toolkit for reducing gun violence via vacant lot greening) and Phlask (map of free water/food/bathrooms). Benefit Decision Toolkit for eligibility screeners. ACT founding member.

name: Code with the Carolinas
description: Carolinas civic tech community. Active through 2024 on Open Sidewalks (sidewalk accessibility mapping) and Zoning Atlas projects. Completed transition from Code for America Brigade Network in 2023. Fiscally sponsored through Open Collective. ACT member.

name: ELGL (Engaging Local Government Leaders)
description: 501(c)(3) connecting innovative local government leaders. 4,800+ members across all 50 states. Runs GovLove Podcast, Top Influencers awards, Analyst Academy, and Public Service Recognition Week. Key community for local gov professionals seeking peers.

name: Florida Community Innovation (FCI)
description: Florida civic tech organization. Published organizational handbook (2025). Florida Resource Map project. AI Fellow program. ACT member.

name: GovLoop
description: Online community of 300,000+ government professionals. Featured Contributor Program, NextGen Government Training Summit, and educational resources on modernization, AI, and workforce. Knowledge-sharing platform connecting public servants across levels.
funding_detail: GovExec Media / Owned by Government Executive Media Group; sponsor-supported content

name: Hack for LA
description: Los Angeles network of civic-minded technologists building digital products with community partners and local government. Global volunteer base (designers, developers, PMs). Maintains Civic Tech Index.

name: Open Austin
description: Austin civic tech community hosting design community of practice, hack nights, and mixers. Sold-out 2025 Public Interest Tech Mixer (37 attendees, 40% people of color). ACT founding member.

name: Open Sacramento
description: Sacramento civic tech group (recently rebranded with new website). Virtual community action nights. ACT member.

name: Open Source San Jose
description: San Jose civic tech collective (joined ACT 2025). Monthly hack nights. Building Tally Up app for CA Dept of Education meal distribution tracking. Open-source, community-driven innovation.

name: OpenOakland
description: Oakland civic tech group building tools for government transparency and community access. ACT member.

name: SF Civic Tech
description: San Francisco civic tech community (fmr. Code for San Francisco, est. 2013). Weekly virtual hack nights. Building SafeHome earthquake risk dashboard. Independent 501(c)(3) since 2024. ACT founding member.

name: Technologists for the Public Good (TPG)
description: 501(c)(6) professional association (est. 2020) for technologists working across government, nonprofits, academia, philanthropy, and civic tech. 134% membership growth in 2023. Runs networking events, tech and design conferences, mentorship programs, and the Tech to Gov Virtual Forum & Job Fair connecting senior technologists with government agencies. Joint statement with ACT on civic tech field direction (2025). Co-hosted State of GovTech 2025 with CivStart in Arlington. Members include government digital service alumni, current federal and state tech staff, and public interest tech practitioners.

name: UChicago Civic Analytics Network (Harris School)
description: Network of chief data officers and analytics leaders in government. Research on data-driven governance and performance management.

name: Ad Hoc
description: Federal digital services firm founded in 2014 from the healthcare.gov rescue. Portfolio includes VA.gov (consolidating 500+ sites), Medicare Plan Finder modernization, and Search.gov. Approximately 700 staff. Focuses on building digital-first agency capacity through embedded product teams.

name: Agile Six
description: Public benefit corporation delivering human-centered digital services to federal agencies. Primary focus on VA digital services and benefits delivery, CDC pandemic readiness, and CMS Medicare modernization. Fully remote, values-driven culture.

name: Behavioural Insights Team (BIT)
description: Global applied behavioral science consultancy founded inside the UK government in 2010, now owned by Nesta (UK innovation charity). US offices in New York and Washington DC. Works with federal, state, and local government agencies to design, test, and iterate on programs using randomized controlled trials and behavioral design. Has run 95+ RCTs with US city governments through the Bloomberg Philanthropies What Works Cities initiative. Partner on UI modernization with NASWA (Nevada DETR 2023). Builds iterative learning and evidence-use capacity inside government agencies.
funding_detail: Government contracts and philanthropy (Bloomberg Philanthropies, What Works Cities); owned by Nesta charity

name: Bloom Works
description: Digital services consultancy delivering user research, service design, engineering, and content strategy to government agencies. Focus on healthcare.gov and social services modernization. Woman-owned small business.

name: Civic Consulting Alliance
description: Chicago-based nonprofit (est. 1985) providing $15-30M/year in pro bono consulting to city and county government. Mobilizes corporate partners (BCG, Deloitte, McKinsey, etc.) for systems-level projects on economic development, education, safety, and health. $200M+ total investment facilitated.
funding_detail: MacArthur Foundation, corporate pro bono partners, philanthropic grants

name: Civic Design Collaborative
description: Human-centered design and civic innovation consultancy working with government agencies on service delivery improvement.

name: CivicActions
description: Twenty years delivering digital services to federal and state agencies - open-source by default and outcomes-focused. Current portfolio includes healthcare.gov, medicare.gov, cms.gov, nsf.gov, and va.gov, with deep practice in agile delivery, user-centered design, accessibility compliance, DevSecOps, and responsible AI-enabled modernization.

name: Civilla
description: Nonprofit design studio dedicated to changing how public-serving institutions work. Human-centered design approach to redesigning government forms, processes, and services. Redesigned Michigan's public benefits application (recognized by Harvard Innovations in Government). Partners with Beeck Center.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants + earned revenue from government partnerships

name: Code for America
description: Leading civic tech nonprofit (15+ yrs). Builds digital tools and changes policies improving criminal justice, safety net, and tax systems. Hosts annual Summit.

name: Coforma
description: Federal digital services firm with strong portfolio in healthcare and civic technology (healthcare.gov, VA, USDS partnerships). SBA-certified.

name: Greater Good Studio
description: Chicago-based design studio applying human-centered design to complex social challenges, including government service delivery, health equity, and criminal justice. Maintains a database of social impact-oriented design professionals and organizations available at greatergoodstudio.com/database. Works with government agencies, nonprofits, and foundations.

name: GreenInfo Network
description: Nonprofit providing GIS, mapping, and data services primarily to government agencies and advocacy organizations. Notable California state agency relationships.

name: Harvard Government Performance Lab (GPL)
description: Embeds full-time fellows in state/local government agencies for 12-36 month reform projects on child welfare, criminal justice, homelessness, housing, and procurement. 112 jurisdictions across 38 states. 278+ projects shifting $7B+ in government spending. Pro bono. Part of Harvard Kennedy School.
funding_detail: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Rockefeller Foundation + Harvard Kennedy School

name: Illinois Digital Service
description: Nonprofit technology partner (fiscally sponsored by Digital Harbor Foundation) offering pro bono digital services to state and local Illinois government agencies. Small team of civic technologists with federal and state government backgrounds. Work spans product management, UX research, service design, software engineering, and data. Current projects include improving public-facing digital services for Illinois agencies. Collaborates with government staff embedded in agency delivery rather than from the outside.
funding_detail: Families and Workers Fund, P33, Origami Works Foundation; fiscally sponsored by Digital Harbor Foundation

name: Mighty Acorn Digital
description: Digital services firm providing product management and delivery support to government agencies.

name: mRelief
description: Nonprofit building tools to simplify access to government benefits. Text and web-based screeners help residents determine eligibility for SNAP, Medicaid, and other programs. Grew out of Chi Hack Night. Partners with city governments and social service orgs.

name: Nava PBC
description: Public benefit corporation delivering agile software development, user-centered design, and cloud engineering to government agencies. Built Healthcare.gov fixes and VA.gov. ~200 employees focused exclusively on government digital services.

name: Partners for Public Good (PPG)
description: Independent nonprofit (launched Mar 2025) spun out of Harvard GPL's procurement research initiative after a decade of incubation. Helps state and local governments improve procurement, staffing, digital infrastructure, and budgeting. Runs Procurement Excellence Network (2,000+ government officials across all 50 states). $5.4B in public spending affected. 200+ local jurisdictions served.

name: Public Policy Lab
description: Nonprofit innovation lab applying human-centered design to government service delivery through direct government agency contracts and grants.

name: Skylight Digital
description: Digital government consultancy delivering agile procurement support, user-centered design, cloud/DevOps, and API-first architecture to federal agencies. HUBZone-certified small business.

name: Third Sector Capital Partners
description: Nonprofit TA firm helping government agencies design and implement outcomes-focused contracting, Pay for Success structures, and data-driven service delivery. Government agencies are primary clients.

name: Truss
description: Federal digital services firm with strong portfolio including IRS Direct File, USWDS contributions, .gov registrar, and VA work. 8(a) SBA certified.

name: U.S. Digital Response (USDR)
description: Matches 11,000+ volunteer technologists with governments needing pro bono technical assistance on digital services, procurement, talent, AI, and language access. 600+ engagements to date across state, local, tribal, and federal governments. Program areas include generative AI, election administration, and talent design. Focus on building lasting government capacity. Runs Digital Service Champions Awards.

name: VotingWorks
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit building open-source, publicly owned voting machines and election auditing software. Only nonprofit building certified voting systems in the US. Deployed in multiple states.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants; nonprofit; only certified nonprofit voting system builder in US

name: Abundance Network
description: National network connecting organizations and advocates advancing abundance-oriented policy reform across housing, energy, and permitting. Functions as a coordinating infrastructure for the broader abundance movement.

name: Accelerator for America
description: Mayoral-led nonprofit co-founded by Eric Garcetti providing cities with technical assistance on federal funding, infrastructure, and economic development. Active in 60+ cities. Supports smart city strategic plans, EDA Tech Hubs applications, and ballot initiative support. Distinctive model: mayors helping mayors navigate federal investment landscape.

name: All Tech Is Human
description: Responsible tech ecosystems org. Slack community, job board, and mentorship program connecting people to careers in public interest technology. Focuses on diversifying the pipeline into tech policy and civic tech roles.

name: ASTHO (Association of State and Territorial Health Officials)
description: National nonprofit representing 59 chief public health officials from 49 states, DC, 5 territories, and 3 Freely Associated States. One of three CDC-designated national partners for the $5B+ Public Health Infrastructure Grant (PHIG, 2022-2027), providing training, technical assistance, workforce development, and data modernization support to 107 funded health departments. Jointly launched the $255M Public Health Data Modernization Implementation Center Program (2024) with NNPHI and PHAB to accelerate health IT standards adoption across state and local health agencies. Develops national public health policy and runs the PH WINS workforce survey in partnership with de Beaumont Foundation.
funding_detail: CDC cooperative agreements (primary, including $155M+ PHIG share) + membership dues from state/territorial health officials + federal grants

name: Bloomberg Cities Network
description: JHU-hosted peer network for city leaders and innovators, created in partnership with Bloomberg Philanthropies. Provides peer networking, idea exchange, training resources, and city solution replication infrastructure. Distinct from the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative (training) and Bloomberg Philanthropies Government Innovation (grantmaking).

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies City Data Alliance
description: Bloomberg Philanthropies program investing 60 million to help cities across the Americas build data infrastructure and AI readiness. 65 cities across 12 countries in current cohort. Structured peer learning model: mayors and chief data officers receive training, tools, and peer network access to advance data-driven governance.

name: City Innovate
description: San Francisco-based nonprofit running the Startup in Residence (STIR) program, connecting startups to government agencies to co-design technology solutions for defined government challenges. Structured procurement reform model that creates a path from co-design to contract. Operates nationally.

name: CivStart
description: Nonprofit govtech accelerator focused on state and local government technology. Six annual cohorts, 71+ startups scaled. Runs a 12-month accelerator, GovTech Lab, and Venture Partner Network connecting startups to investors. Most recent cohort focused on AI in local government in partnership with NLC and GovAI Coalition.
funding_detail: Foundation grants; government and corporate partnerships

name: Colorado Smart Cities Alliance
description: Statewide coalition of government, business, and academic partners convening around smart city technology adoption in Colorado. Runs challenge-based procurement programs, pilots, and the Smart Futures Lab accelerator. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: GovAI Coalition
description: Coalition of 2,000+ public servants from 700+ local, county, and state governments advocating for responsible public sector AI. Historically led by City of San Jose, but transitioned to full non-profit status. Produces AI policy templates, vendor AI FactSheets, use case libraries, and AI Contract Hub. Open to government, academia, and industry.
funding_detail: City of San Jose leads; member contributions; philanthropic support

name: HSITAG (Human Services IT Advisory Group)
description: The Human Services IT Advisory Group (HSITAG) is a nonprofit trade association (under CompTIA) serving as the bridge between health and human services IT vendors and government HHS agencies. Founded 1993, 123 member companies. Trusted advisor to federal and state HHS technology procurement officials. Key node for human services technology, benefits delivery, and HHS IT problem statements.
funding_detail: Member dues from 123 technology companies; CompTIA affiliation

name: Illinois Smart City and Region Association (ISCRA)
description: 501c3 nonprofit association bringing municipalities and technology vendors together in a neutral forum to advance smart city and region initiatives across Illinois. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: KC Digital Drive
description: Kansas City-based nonprofit founded in 2012 to make the region a digital leader. Runs Code for KC, convenes the KC Coalition for Digital Inclusion, and hosts civic tech and smart city programs. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: Leading Cities
description: Global city network operating AcceliGOV, a structured program that deploys vetted smart city technology solutions into municipalities through 90-day paid pilots. Government is the customer; Leading Cities handles sourcing, vetting, onboarding, and deployment support. Clinton Global Initiative partner. 32+ projects completed; goal of 100 resilience projects in 100 communities by 2030. Focus areas: coastal resilience, flood risk, water management, mobility, and urban infrastructure.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants + corporate partnerships + city engagement fees

name: NASCIO (National Association of State Chief Information Officers)
description: The primary peer network, research body, and voice for state CIOs. Conducts the annual State CIO Survey (51 state/territory responses in 2025) and publishes State CIO Top 10 Priorities. Partners with McKinsey, EY, and Deloitte on major research initiatives including GenAI adoption, cybersecurity, and data quality. Hosts two annual conferences in DC and a fall gathering. Produces the definitive annual mapping of state technology priorities. NASCIO State IT Recognition Awards annually highlight the most innovative state IT programs.
funding_detail: State membership dues + corporate associate program + conference revenue

name: National Association of State Workforce Agencies (NASWA)
description: National nonprofit (est. 1937) representing all 50 state workforce agencies, DC, and US territories. Operates the UI Information Technology Support Center (UI ITSC), the Workforce ITSC, UI SIDES (State Information Data Exchange System), UI ICON (Interstate Connection Network), and the National Labor Exchange -- the backbone technology and standards infrastructure for state UI and workforce systems. Provides technology consulting, training, and policy advocacy to state agencies. Partnered with Georgetown Beeck Center and DOL on the Open UI Initiative. CESER (Center for Employment Security Education and Research) is its 501(c)(3) research and consulting arm.
funding_detail: Membership dues from 50 state workforce agencies + federal contracts and cooperative agreements (DOL); CESER 501(c)(3) arm receives federal grants

name: NNPHI (National Network of Public Health Institutes)
description: National membership association representing 40+ state and regional public health institutes. One of three CDC-designated national partners for the $5B+ Public Health Infrastructure Grant (PHIG, 2022-2027). Provides technical assistance to health departments through nine Regional Innovation Hubs covering all 50 states. Operates the National Coordinating Center for Public Health Training (NCCPHT). Co-leads PHIG national evaluation with PHAB. Co-launched the $255M Public Health Data Modernization Implementation Center Program in 2024 to accelerate HL7 FHIR and related health IT standards in state and local health agencies.
funding_detail: CDC cooperative agreements (primary, including PHIG share) + member fees + federal and foundation grants (Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, HHS Office of Minority Health)

name: North Texas Innovation Alliance (NTXIA)
description: 501c3 regional consortium of 50+ municipalities, agencies, corporations, and academic institutions across North Texas. Facilitates call-for-innovation programs, procurement reform, and smart region strategy. Largest initiative of its kind in the US.

name: Partnership Fund for NYC
description: NYC-based evergreen fund running structured challenge programs connecting early-stage startups to public agencies (MTA, Port Authority, NYCHA) for proof-of-concept pilots and procurement pathways. Has brokered 32 million+ in government contracts. Ecosystem intermediary bridging GovTech vendors and city government.

name: SETDA (State Educational Technology Directors Association)
description: Principal national membership association representing U.S. state and territorial educational technology and digital learning leaders. Members are state government officials (state ed agency CIOs and ed tech directors). Publishes the annual State EdTech Trends report (47-state survey); produces procurement guidance; advocates for federal ed tech funding (E-rate, Title II-A); and builds capacity of state education agencies to adopt technology responsibly. Founded 2001; 25+ years of operation.
funding_detail: State education agency membership dues + foundation grants (Siegel Family Endowment, Google.org) + federal education grants

name: Smart North Florida (SNF)
description: Nonprofit dedicated to harnessing regional collaboration, data coordination, and smart technologies to improve Northeast Florida economic competitiveness, sustainability, and quality of life. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: Southern Arizona Smart Region (Regional Partnering Center)
description: Greater Tucson regional smart city initiative led by the Regional Partnering Center, a public-private partnership. Works to build economic competitiveness and quality of life through collaborative smart region strategy. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: The Connective
description: Greater Phoenix smart region consortium launched in 2019. Partners public sector, academia, industry, and civic institutions to co-design and deploy technology solutions for regional challenges. Problem-driven model: cities surface needs, the Connective facilitates solution development.

name: US Ignite
description: National nonprofit (NSF-originated) providing technical assistance and capacity-building to communities navigating broadband deployment and smart city development. Manages federal funding identification tools, runs community programs including Project OVERCOME, and operates the PAWR advanced wireless research platform.
funding_detail: NSF, Schmidt Futures, Knight Foundation; federal program funding

name: AAAS S&T Policy Fellowships
description: 1-2 year fellowships placing scientists and engineers in federal agencies and Congress. Expanded AI tracks. 3,500+ alumni since 1973.

name: California Capital Fellows Program
description: Four fellowships (Assembly, Senate, Executive, Judicial) placing 64 fellows/year at highest levels of CA state government for 10-11 months. Fellows assist legislators, senior executive staff, and court administrators on policy. Nationally recognized.

name: CCST (California Council on Science and Technology)
description: Hybrid research and fellowship organization placing 10-15 PhD-level fellows annually into the California Legislature and Executive Branch. One of the longest-running state-level science fellowship programs in the US.

name: CivicSpark (AmeriCorps)
description: 11-month AmeriCorps fellowship placing ~150 fellows/year in local governments and community orgs for capacity building on climate, housing, water, transportation, public health. 1,000+ alumni since 2014. Expanding beyond CA/CO/WA to all states starting 2025.
funding_detail: AmeriCorps federal funding + local agency cost-share ($37,500/fellow)

name: Coding it Forward Fellowship
description: 10-week paid summer placement of early-career technologists in federal, state, and local government. Five tracks: data, design, product, software, cybersecurity. 700+ alumni.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment, McGovern Foundation, Pivotal Ventures

name: Cornell Tech PiTech Initiative
description: PhD Impact Fellowships, Visiting Practitioner's Program, and PiTech Impact Studio for graduate students working on public interest technology.

name: Coro Fellows Program in Public Affairs
description: 7-9 month full-time experiential leadership program. Fellows rotate through placements in government, nonprofit, business, and labor. 80+ year track record. 15,000+ alumni including US Senators and elected officials. Programs in LA, SF, NYC, Pittsburgh, St. Louis.

name: DC Capital City Fellows Program (CCFP)
description: 18-month mayoral initiative placing recent masters graduates in DC government agencies. Three 6-month rotations across government operations, health/human services, public safety, planning, or education. Entry salary ~$62K.

name: FUSE Corps
description: 1-year executive fellowship placing experienced professionals in city/county agencies for strategic projects. 250+ projects across 42 cities/18 states.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Irvine Foundation

name: Georgetown McCourt Tech & Policy Visiting Fellows
description: Semester-long visiting fellowship for tech policy practitioners at Georgetown McCourt School. Multiple USDS alumni and former federal tech officials in inaugural 2025 cohort. Fellows write policy essays, mentor students, and conduct research.

name: Govern for America (GFA)
description: Two-year paid fellowship placing recent graduates in high-impact state/local government roles. Published AI x Talent research for states.

name: Harvard Ash Center Democracy Fellowships
description: Financial support for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers studying democratic governance, innovation in government, and civic technology. Part of the Ash Center's Program on Democratic Governance.

name: Horizon Institute for Public Service
description: Training and fellowships for scientists and technologists entering government service.

name: Judicial Innovation Fellowship (Georgetown)
description: 1-year fellowship placing technologists, designers, and user testers in state, local, tribal, and territorial courts to build data infrastructure, simplify processes, and improve access to justice. Inaugural cohort 2023-24. Incubated at Georgetown Law's Institute for Technology Law & Policy.

name: Lead for America
description: Fellowship placing young leaders in local governments and nonprofits in their hometowns, with focus on rural and underserved communities. AmeriCorps-backed. Runs American Connection Corps, a digital inclusion program placing fellows in rural communities. Builds local government capacity from within through long-term place-based commitment.

name: Media Democracy Fund Fellowships

description: Statewide IT strategy and digital services division within the Arizona Department of Administration, led by State CIO J.R. Sloan. name: Arlington County Digital Innovation

description: Division within the Bureau of Indian Affairs Office of Trust Services providing technical assistance to Tribal Nations on broadband, electromagnetic spectrum leasing, wireless services, and digital capacity on tribal lands. name: Boston Department of Innovation and Technology (DoIT)
description: City of Boston's enterprise technology organization serving 18,000+ city employees and hundreds of thousands of constituents. Manages BOS:311, digital services delivery, the Wicked Free Wi-Fi program, and a Digital Equity Fund. ~150 employees under Mayor Michelle Wu's Innovation and Technology Cabinet.

name: California Office of Data & Innovation (ODI)
description: Statewide digital services team delivering user research, content design, data analytics, and plain language guidance across CA state agencies.

name: Chicago Department of Technology and Innovation (DTI)
description: New citywide technology department established under Mayor Brandon Johnson (est. late 2023) - a deliberate rethinking of Chicago's IT approach. CIO/Commissioner Nick Lucius confirmed by City Council 48-0 in May 2024. Lucius previously served as Chicago's chief data officer and CTO. Maintains the Chicago Design System and coordinates technology across all city departments under a unified strategy focused on reducing operational complexity and improving resident-facing digital service delivery.

name: City and County of Denver - Peak Academy & Technology Services
description: Denver leads in two distinct dimensions of city capacity. Denver Peak Academy (within the Budget & Management Office) has trained 11,000+ Denver employees and participants from 350+ governments in lean process improvement since 2012, saving the city $75M+. OIT recently created separate CDO and CISO roles under CIO Suma Nallapati.

name: CMS Digital Service (DSAC)

description: Dedicated state AI office. Published AI Roadmap and Governance Framework. $15M additional for cybersecurity/AI. Cloud-first initiative with AI integration.

name: Hennepin County Digital Experience (DX)
description: Digital services and experience team for Hennepin County, Minnesota (Minneapolis metro). Verified active with 21-25 FTE. One of the largest county-level digital service teams in the US.

name: House Digital Service (HDS)
description: Digital service team for the US House of Representatives, established 2019. Serves the legislative branch, distinct from executive branch digital service teams.

name: Illinois Department of Innovation & Technology (DoIT)
description: State enterprise IT agency created by statute in 2018, serving 36 client agencies directly and 90+ government entities statewide including high-speed broadband to 610 school districts. Led by State CIO/Secretary Sanjay Gupta (former USDOJ and SBA CIO; Senate-confirmed 2024). Key 2024-25 initiatives include enterprise AI governance, benefits modernization for SNAP and Medicaid, digital driver's licenses via Apple Wallet, and a new Central Computing Facility replacing 1970s-era legacy data center infrastructure.

name: InnovateOhio Platform (Ohio Office of Information Technology)
description: Ohio's enterprise digital modernization initiative within the Department of Administrative Services' Office of Information Technology, led by State CIO Katrina Flory (GovTech Top 25 2024). Delivers OH|ID statewide single sign-on (used by nearly half of all Ohioans), data analytics, fraud detection, and a new content management system across hundreds of agency websites and apps. Added digital driver's licenses to Apple Wallet in 2024. Received NASCIO State IT Recognition Award for cybersecurity excellence in 2025.

name: Lebanon, NH

name: Los Angeles Information Technology Agency (ITA)
description: City of LA's enterprise technology department - 442 IT professionals across 18 divisions delivering 366 services on a $90M annual operating budget. Roadmap (June 2024) and 2024-2025 Strategic Plan focused on digital transformation, AI governance, and smart city infrastructure for the 2026 World Cup, 2027 Super Bowl, and 2028 Olympics.

Co-leading a landmark multi-agency AI partnership with Anthropic and Percepta - backed by Rockefeller Foundation - to modernize benefits delivery, environmental permitting, and housing access. Published 2025 AI Enablement Strategy and AI Study Roadmap covering 12 critical domains.

Authorized by Gov. Healey's FutureTech Act of 2024 ($110M bond authorization). Ranked #1 in the nation by the Center for Digital Government's GovX Awards in 2024.
