funding_detail: LP-funded PE; ~$3.9B total invested since 1983; govtech is named sector focus

name: Commonweal Ventures
description: Early-stage VC fund investing in technology companies serving government customers with a focus on public safety and state/local government. Portfolio includes Multitude Insights (law enforcement collaboration tools), Deckard Technologies (AI-driven municipal tax compliance), and others serving SLED markets. Participated in Starbridge Series A (2025).
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; undisclosed fund size; seed and early-stage focus on public safety and govtech

name: Govtech Fund (Ron Bouganim)
description: First venture capital fund dedicated exclusively to government technology startups, founded by Ron Bouganim. Makes seed-stage investments ($250K-$500K) in companies selling technology directly to government. ~$50M across two funds. Portfolio includes Mark43 (public safety), SeamlessDocs/GovOS (digital forms), SmartProcure (procurement intelligence), and Merit (verified credentials). Bouganim serves on board of Merit. Strong NASCIO and govtech conference presence.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; ~$50M AUM across two funds; seed stage ($250K-$500K checks)

name: Govtech Ventures (Rachel Stern)
description: Early-stage VC fund (est. 2024) dedicated exclusively to modernizing state and local government. Founded by Rachel Stern, who was the first investor in PayIt and co-founded InState Partners at Advantage Capital. Raising a $15M inaugural fund targeting pre-seed through seed-plus with LPs including govtech founders and family offices. Portfolio includes Polco, Streamline, and Ladris. Focused specifically on SLED market operators.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; ~$15M inaugural fund (fundraising 2024-2025); pre-seed to seed-plus stage

name: Great Hill Partners
description: Boston-based PE firm that built a deliberate govtech investment strategy. Hired Granicus co-founder Tom Spengler as Executive-in-Residence to source govtech deals. In 2025 led the majority recapitalization of Vision Government Solutions - property tax and appraisal software serving 900+ jurisdictions - alongside Weatherford Capital. Strong track record of govtech platform investments and exits.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; $12B+ total capital raised across funds; govtech is named vertical

name: IQT (In-Q-Tel)
description: In-Q-Tel (IQT) is the strategic investor for the US intelligence community, founded 1999 by the CIA. Invests in commercial technology companies to bring cutting-edge capabilities to national security agencies. Portfolio spans AI, cybersecurity, data analytics, and quantum computing. Bridge between Silicon Valley and the intelligence community. The original govtech investor.
funding_detail: CIA and US intelligence community funding

name: J2 Ventures
description: Defense and national security-focused venture fund investing in software and technology for government and defense agencies. Government is the explicit primary customer. Part of the emerging defense tech VC ecosystem alongside IQT and Paladin.

name: JFF Ventures
description: The impact venture arm of JFF (Jobs for the Future). Invests in workforce development and education technology where government workforce programs (WIOA, Perkins, WIA) are often the primary customer. Bridges JFF's policy and research work with technology investment. Key node for workforce development, economic mobility, and human capital problem statements.

name: Kapor Capital
description: Oakland-based early-stage VC (est. 1999) investing in tech startups that close gaps of access for low-income communities and communities of color. Notable govtech investments include Promise (government payment modernization) and Aclima (air quality monitoring for regulators and municipalities). $224M+ AUM across multiple funds. Co-founder Mitchell Kapor is a longtime civic tech philanthropist. Portfolio of 170+ active investments with 4 unicorns and 6 IPOs.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $224M+ AUM; Kapor Capital Fund III; seed stage focus

name: Omidyar Network
description: Philanthropic investment firm that makes both grants and equity investments at the intersection of responsible technology and governance. Funds TechCongress and responsible technology initiatives with an explicit focus on ensuring the digital revolution serves shared power and prosperity. Has deployed $2B+ to 700+ organizations spanning nonprofits and for-profits. Spun out Luminate (grants) and retained the investing arm as Omidyar Network.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar personal capital; ~$2B deployed across grants and equity investments

name: Paladin Capital Group
description: Washington DC-based VC focused on cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection technology for government and defense customers. Portfolio includes companies serving DHS, DoD, and civilian agencies. Government is the explicit primary customer. Key node for cybersecurity and critical infrastructure problem statements.

name: Serent Capital
description: Growth-focused PE firm with a dedicated GovTech investment team. Five govtech platform investments in four years including BS&A Software (municipal ERP, acquired 2021), First Due (fire and EMS software), GovWorx (911 quality assurance), and Pondera Solutions (fraud detection for government benefits, exited to Thomson Reuters). Targets profitable, recurring-revenue cloud SaaS companies selling to state and local agencies.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; multiple funds since 2008; $3B+ total capital under management

name: Socium Ventures
description: Evergreen venture fund backed by Cox Enterprises with $600M+ committed across two funds (Fund II: $300M closed Oct 2024). Notable govtech investment includes Carbyne - next-generation 911 and emergency response platform - which was acquired by Axon in November 2025 for $625M. Cox Enterprises is also the majority acquirer of OpenGov ($1.8B, 2024), giving Socium strategic alignment with govtech through its parent. Portfolio also includes health, enterprise software, and AI companies.
funding_detail: Cox Enterprises-backed evergreen fund; $300M Fund II (Oct 2024); $600M+ total committed

name: Town Hall Ventures
description: Venture fund explicitly focused on health and human services technology where government is the primary paying customer. Invests in companies serving Medicaid, Medicare, SNAP, and other public benefit programs. Key investor node for benefits delivery, health equity, and government health program modernization problem statements.

name: Weatherford Capital (Will Weatherford)
description: Family-owned PE firm founded in 2015 by former Florida House Speaker Will Weatherford. Seven govtech platform investments since inception including PayIt (digital government payments), OpenGov ($1.8B exit to Cox Enterprises, 2024), SOMA Global (public safety), and BusPatrol (school bus safety). Closed $300M Fund II in 2025. Deep government relationships - rooted in Weatherford's legislative background - as a core value-add for portfolio companies navigating procurement.
funding_detail: Family-owned PE; $300M Fund II closed 2025; $1B+ AUM across two funds

name: Annie E. Casey Foundation
description: Major funder of Georgetown Beeck Center. Focus on child welfare, juvenile justice, and family economic success; all areas where government delivery capacity is critical. Funds community-based organizations and government agencies improving child/family outcomes through data and technology.

name: Arnold Ventures
description: Funds evidence-based government reform including Results for America and government performance initiatives. Focus on criminal justice, health, evidence-based implementation.

name: Ballmer Group (Steve & Connie Ballmer)
description: Funds data-driven systems change for economic mobility. Key funder of GovEx/JHU Centers for Civic Impact. Supports USAFacts (gov data transparency platform Steve Ballmer personally launched). Large-scale state partnerships - $1B+ commitment to WA state early childhood. Focus on evidence-based government, workforce development, and using data to improve government services.
funding_detail: Steve Ballmer personal wealth (fmr. Microsoft CEO)

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies: Government Innovation
description: Major funder of city-level government innovation. Funds Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative, Bloomberg Center for Cities, What Works Cities (via Results for America), Data-Smart City Solutions, i-teams.
funding_detail: Bloomberg LP profits; Michael Bloomberg personal wealth

name: Blue Meridian Partners
description: Funder collaborative housed at Edna McConnell Clark Foundation that finds and scales solutions for economic mobility. Major Ballmer Group partner. Funds organizations at the intersection of nonprofit service delivery and government systems change. Relevant because many grantees work directly with government agencies on benefits delivery, workforce development, and child welfare systems.
funding_detail: Ballmer Group, Sergey Brin Family Foundation, Edna McConnell Clark Foundation + others; grants-based, not equity

name: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI)
description: LLC blending grants and investments. Funded FUSE Corps. Community program supports housing, health, and economic development in San Mateo County/Bay Area. Note: CZI significantly restructured in Feb 2025 - cut social advocacy funding, DEI teams, and shifted focus to AI in science and education. State capacity relevance is narrower now than pre-2025.
funding_detail: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan personal wealth; operates as LLC

name: Craig Newmark Philanthropies
description: Founded by craigslist founder. Major funder of Aspen Policy Academy / Tech Policy Hub since its founding. Supports cybersecurity, trustworthy journalism, and public interest technology pipeline. Pragmatic, hands-on funder with focus on infrastructure for civic tech.

name: Data.org
description: Nonprofit building the field of data for social impact. Capacity Accelerator Network provides training and resources for organizations using data to improve public services. Inclusive Growth and Recovery Challenge funds data-driven solutions.
funding_detail: Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth + philanthropic

name: de Beaumont Foundation
description: Bethesda-based private foundation (est. 1998, fully endowed 2010) focused on strengthening state and local health department capacity and the public health workforce. Operates as an engaged programmatic funder -- identifies gaps, builds tools, and convenes partners rather than accepting proposals. Key programs: PH WINS (nationally representative survey of 10,000+ public health workers, in partnership with ASTHO); Public Health Forward modernization roadmap (with Bipartisan Policy Center); Public Health Workforce Calculator (with CDC and PHNCI); and the IMPACT collaborative pairing health departments with private sector partners. Convened the National Consortium for Public Health Workforce Development (sunseted 2023 as CDC PHIG absorbed the function).
funding_detail: Fully endowed private foundation (Pierre de Beaumont estate); does not accept unsolicited proposals

name: Democracy Fund (Omidyar Group)
description: Nonpartisan foundation focused on effective and accountable government as one of four pillars. Funds congressional modernization orgs (POPVOX Foundation, Lincoln Network), government transparency, and legislative branch capacity-building. $200+ grants/year. Doubling down on democracy defense in 2025-2026.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar / Omidyar Group

name: Emerson Collective (Laurene Powell Jobs)
description: LLC (~$28B AUM) blending VC, philanthropy, and advocacy. Invested in OpenGov (pre-acquisition). Education reform (XQ Institute, College Track) and immigration policy are core verticals where EC works to reshape government systems. Founded Chicago CRED (gun violence intervention with government) and E Pluribus Unum (civic engagement in the South). Strong state and local policy advocacy capacity.
funding_detail: Powell Jobs personal wealth; Waverley Street Foundation committed $3.5B over 10 years

name: Families and Workers Fund
description: 135M+ pooled funder collaborative (40+ funders including Ford Foundation, Schmidt Futures, Rockefeller, Annie E. Casey, Open Society, MacKenzie Scott) funding civic tech, public benefits delivery modernization, and government innovation alongside workforce policy. Runs the Public Benefit Innovation Fund (PBIF), an open call for AI-enabled benefits delivery solutions. Key funder node connecting much of the benefits tech and government delivery ecosystem.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Schmidt Futures, Rockefeller Foundation, Annie E. Casey, Open Society Foundations, MacKenzie Scott, and 35+ co-funders

name: Ford Foundation
description: Major funder of public interest technology ecosystem. Co-convenes PIT-UN. Funds Coding it Forward, FUSE Corps, Aspen Policy Academy, Data & Society, Ash Center endowment, PIT Infrastructure Fund.

name: Gates Foundation
description: Funds GovEx/JHU Centers for Civic Impact. Supports government data capacity for public health and education policy. K-12 and public health data systems work often intersects with state/local government capacity. Large-scale but government modernization is a secondary rather than primary focus.

name: Google.org
description: Google's philanthropic arm. Funded Decoded Futures AI capacity-building for NYC nonprofits ($1M grant). Supports AI for social good, digital skills training, and civic technology projects. Corporate partner for government AI pilots (e.g., Seattle, Boston traffic optimization).

name: Hewlett Foundation
description: Co-convenes PIT-UN. Funds TechCongress, public interest technology infrastructure, and government performance programs.

name: Irvine Foundation (James Irvine Foundation)
description: California-focused funder. Supports FUSE Corps. Focus on economic and political inclusion in California; funds orgs that strengthen civic participation and government responsiveness at state and local levels.

name: Knight Foundation
description: Invests in civic engagement, data-driven governance, and smart city strategies. $4M+ investment in 8 orgs using tech/data to strengthen public services. Funds Harvard Data-Smart City Solutions, GovEx/JHU, San Jose AI partnerships, and Knight Emerging City Champions fellowship (micro-grants for young civic innovators in 8 Knight resident communities). Focus on mid-size US cities.

name: Luminate (Omidyar Group)
description: Global foundation focused on civic empowerment, data and digital rights, financial transparency, and independent media. Funds orgs working on government transparency, open data, and citizen participation. Spun out of Omidyar Network's Governance & Citizen Engagement initiative in 2018.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar / Omidyar Group

name: MacArthur Foundation
description: Major funder of Civic Consulting Alliance ($6M+ since 2003). Supports government accountability, criminal justice reform, and community development orgs that work with local government. Also funds Data & Society and investigative journalism that surfaces government capacity issues.

name: Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth / Mastercard Impact Fund
description: Corporate philanthropy arm. Co-funds PIT-UN with Ford and Hewlett. Funds data.org and data-for-social-impact initiatives. Supports government digital inclusion and financial access programs.

name: New Profit
description: Pioneer venture philanthropy fund investing in social entrepreneurs tackling civic engagement and government service delivery. In 2024 invested $2.6M across 24 organizations. Build Investments provide $1.5M multi-year unrestricted grants paired with deal partners. Portfolio includes public service pipeline orgs like Latinas Represent.

name: NextLadder Ventures
description: $1B+ initiative launched July 2025 by Ballmer Group, Gates Foundation, Stand Together, Valhalla Foundation, and John Overdeck. Invests in entrepreneurs building tech-enabled solutions helping low-income Americans navigate government systems and economic barriers. Uses a mix of grants, equity, and revenue-based financing over a 15-year horizon. Relevant to state capacity as it funds the interface layer between government benefits systems and residents.
funding_detail: $1B+ committed across founding coalition over 15 years; mix of grants, equity, and revenue-based financing

name: Open Philanthropy
description: Major funder of Niskanen Center (state capacity work) and immigration reform advocacy. Research-driven grantmaking. AI governance and policy is growing focus area. Funds GiveDirectly and evidence-based policy research that intersects with government delivery.
funding_detail: Cari Tuna and Dustin Moskovitz (Facebook co-founder)

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
description: Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Govern for America, and orgs advancing responsible AI and data use in public sector.

name: Pivotal Ventures (Melinda French Gates)
description: Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Govern for America, and pathways for underrepresented technologists in government.

name: Public Benefit Innovation Fund
description: Pooled grantmaking vehicle housed at Center for Civic Futures. They provide seed funding and technical support for researchers, nonprofits, academic labs, startups, and technologists working to improve social service delivery.
funding_detail: Gates Foundation, Ballmer Group, Renaissance Philanthropy,  Digital Harbor Foundation

name: Public Interest Technology Infrastructure Fund (PIT Fund)
description: Pooled grantmaking vehicle housed at New Venture Fund. Dedicated to building the PIT ecosystem; funds talent pipeline orgs like Coding it Forward ($550K), Govern for America, #BlackTechFutures ($250K), AAAS AI fellowships ($250K), PIT hubs ($200K each), and Data & Society. Funded by Ford, Siegel, McGovern, Pivotal, Schmidt Futures.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Siegel, McGovern, Pivotal Ventures, Schmidt Futures

name: Raikes Foundation
description: Co-funds PIT-UN. Founded by Jeff Raikes (fmr. Microsoft exec, fmr. Gates Foundation CEO). Supports education, youth development, and public interest technology pipeline programs.

name: Robin Hood Foundation
description: NYC's largest local poverty-fighting philanthropy. Seeded Decoded Futures AI capacity-building for nonprofits delivering public services.

name: Rockefeller Foundation
description: Launched AI Readiness Project (Nov 2025) expanding to all 50 states. Funds state/local government AI capacity-building and digital inclusion.

name: Schmidt Futures
description: Philanthropic initiative (Eric & Wendy Schmidt) making grants and investments at intersection of talent and technology. Funded Social Safety Net Product Studio, USDR, FAS, PIT-UN, benefits access modernization.
funding_detail: Schmidt family wealth; operates as LLC

name: Siegel Family Endowment
description: Committed $20M to PIT ecosystem. Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Aspen Policy Academy, Data & Society, New America PIT.

name: Thierer Family Foundation
description: Chicago-based foundation that funds technology capacity for nonprofits and government-adjacent organizations. Founded Vivery, a food access technology platform now used by 21+ food banks. Focus on technology as a lever for social impact, with emphasis on food access, benefits navigation, and digital inclusion. Grants technology solutions to nonprofits at no cost through the Vivery Community model.

name: Valhalla Foundation
description: Philanthropy focused on measurable improvement in children's lives through early childhood development, K-12 education, and data science. Co-founder of NextLadder Ventures. Invests in data-driven approaches to improving government-run systems particularly in education and child welfare. Collaborative philanthropy model emphasizing cross-funder coordination.

name: AI Now Institute of Technology
description: Independent policy research institute (est. 2017 at NYU; fully independent since 2022) studying the social implications of AI with a focus on power concentration, public accountability, and government use of AI. Annual Landscape Report is a field-defining publication on AI governance. Leadership advised the FTC on AI in 2021-22. Research covers government use of AI in benefits systems, hiring, criminal justice, and public services - making it directly relevant to state capacity accountability. Explicitly refuses corporate tech funding to maintain independence. 2025 Landscape Report: "Artificial Power" focused on reclaiming public control over AI trajectory. Funded by Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Omidyar Network, Luminate.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Omidyar Network, Luminate; no corporate tech industry funding

name: Aspen Institute
description: Nonpartisan forum for values-based leadership. Relevant programs include Aspen Policy Academy (see Training segment), Aspen Digital (tech policy), and various governance convenings. Broader than state capacity but significant convening power at leadership level.
funding_detail: Broad philanthropic base; major foundation support; event revenue

name: Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC)
description: Centrist think tank founded by former Senate majority leaders from both parties. Governance program focuses on congressional capacity, executive branch management, and government modernization. Technology project examines AI governance and digital government policy.
funding_detail: Bipartisan philanthropic base; foundation and corporate support

name: Brookings: Center for Technology Innovation
description: Policy research on AI governance, digital government, tech talent, and government modernization. Congressional testimony.

name: Building State Capability (BSC) - Harvard Kennedy School
description: Applied research program at Harvard Kennedy School led by Prof. Matt Andrews, pioneering the Problem Driven Iterative Adaptation (PDIA) methodology for escaping government capability traps. Foundational scholarship on why government reforms fail (isomorphic mimicry, premature load-bearing) and how to build real implementation capacity. Has trained 4,850+ practitioners in 157 countries including US state and local officials. Offers online courses, executive education, and PDIA coaching. Most directly relevant academic program to the core question of how governments build implementation capacity.
funding_detail: Harvard Kennedy School endowment + earned revenue from executive education

name: Center for a New American Security (CNAS)
description: Bipartisan national security think tank. Technology and National Security program researches AI, emerging tech, and defense innovation. [NOTE: Primarily defense-focused. State capacity relevance is limited to where defense tech/AI governance intersects with broader government modernization.]
funding_detail: Broad bipartisan donor base; foundation and government grants

name: Center for Democracy and Technology (CDT)
description: Nonpartisan 501(c)(3) (est. 1994) promoting democratic values by shaping technology policy with a focus on individual rights. CDT AI Governance Lab (launched May 2023, director Miranda Bogen) is the most state capacity-relevant unit - advises policymakers on AI auditing, safety, and accountability; publishes technical guidance on bias measurement, AI documentation, fairness assessments, and government use of AI in benefits, education, and law enforcement. Works directly with federal agencies and regulators. Hosted fellowships for researchers on algorithmic fairness and AI safety. In 2024 the Lab analyzed open foundation model risks with Stanford HAI and published reports on AI assurance and action-taking AI agents.
funding_detail: Foundation-funded; Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, and others; no corporate tech funding

name: Center for Information Technology Policy (CITP, Princeton)
description: The Center for Information Technology Policy (CITP) at Princeton University is an interdisciplinary research center studying the intersection of technology and public life. Research areas include election security, AI regulation, algorithmic accountability, surveillance, and digital rights. Notable alumni pipeline into USDS, FTC, and congressional tech policy offices. Bridges technical and policy communities.

name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET)
description: The Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET) at Georgetown University is a think tank focused on AI and national security policy. Produces policy analysis for DoD, Congress, and the intelligence community. Founded by former IARPA director Jason Matheny. Key node for AI governance, national competitiveness, and government AI adoption problem statements.

name: Center for Tribal Digital Sovereignty (ASU / NCAI)
description: First and only center in the US dedicated to helping tribal governments build digital sovereignty plans. Launched June 2024 as a partnership between the American Indian Policy Institute (AIPI) at ASU Law and the National Congress of American Indians. Serves all 574 federally recognized Tribal Nations. Provides research, capacity-building support, and policy advocacy. Publishes AI governance frameworks for tribal contexts (Feb 2026). Co-hosts the annual Wiring the Rez conference (227 participants from 44 Tribal nations in 2025). Seed funding from Ford Foundation and Google.org. Acts as clearinghouse for tribal digital sovereignty resources - broadband governance, data sovereignty, spectrum management, and tribal tech codes.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation + Google.org seed funding; ASU and NCAI foundational support; seeking additional philanthropic partners

name: Centre for Public Impact (CPI)
description: Global not-for-profit providing government reimagining consulting, adaptive leadership coaching, and legitimacy frameworks.
funding_detail: BCG Foundation (founded by BCG; now independently operated); diversified philanthropic base

name: Council of State Governments (CSG)
description: Founded 1933 - the nation's only nonpartisan organization serving all three branches of state government. Publishes the annual Book of the States (comprehensive statistical reference on state government) and Capitol Ideas magazine. New CSG 50-State Scan policy research series (2025) examines top priorities including government performance and reform. CSG Justice Center develops research-driven criminal justice reform strategies. Six regional offices support state legislators, governors, and judicial officials with research, TA, and peer exchange.
funding_detail: State appropriations (population-based dues) + federal grants + foundation grants

name: Data & Society
description: Research institute studying social implications of data and AI. Public Technology Leadership Collaborative connects tech experts with government leaders.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: Data Foundation
description: Nonprofit that tracks open government data policy across all 50 states and publishes the annual State of Data Ownership report. Runs the Data Coalition, advocating for federal and state data infrastructure standards. Meaningful node for open data and data infrastructure problem statements.
funding_detail: Foundation grants; member dues from Data Coalition

name: Foundation for American Innovation
description: Center-right innovation policy think tank. Senior Fellows program places technologists in congressional offices. Key 2024-25 work: GAO reform proposals, AI governance research, congressional tech capacity. Runs The Dynamist podcast and AI Policy Leadership Network with CNAS and Horizon.

name: Georgetown Beeck Center
description: Provides technical assistance, communities of practice, and practitioner training on digital government, data governance, and AI for state/local agencies. Runs Digital Government Hub.
funding_detail: Georgetown + Annie E. Casey Foundation, Bloomberg, others

name: Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA)
description: National professional association of 30,000+ state, provincial, and local government finance officers (est. 1906). Publishes the authoritative Governmental Accounting, Auditing, and Financial Reporting guide (GAAFR/"Blue Book") and Government Finance Review magazine. Research and Consulting Center is the market leader in helping local governments procure ERP and financial systems - has assisted 450+ governments with system selection and contract negotiation. Runs best practice award programs (CAFR, budget awards) and leadership training. 1-year Research Fellows program for recent UChicago graduates.
funding_detail: Member dues + conference revenue + consulting fees + publication sales

name: GovEx / Johns Hopkins Centers for Civic Impact
description: Bloomberg Center for Government Excellence at Johns Hopkins. Provides technical assistance, coaching, and training to help cities use data, analytics, and AI. Runs City Data Alliance and GovEx Academy (online courses). Worked with 140+ cities. CDOs-in-Residence program.
funding_detail: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Ballmer Group, Knight Foundation, Gates Foundation + JHU

name: Harvard Ash Center for Democratic Governance and Innovation
description: Leading academic center for government innovation and democratic governance at Harvard Kennedy School. $50M Ford Foundation endowment. Programs include: Innovations in American Government Awards (recognizing excellence in state/local government since 1985); Data-Smart City Solutions (Bloomberg-funded, covering city data and AI); Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation (technology and democratic institutions); and Harvard Project on American Indian Economic Development. Houses the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative executive education program.
funding_detail: $50M Ford Foundation endowment + Bloomberg Philanthropies ($32M for City Leadership Initiative) + Harvard Kennedy School

name: IBM Center for the Business of Government
description: Independent research center (est. 1998 as PricewaterhouseCoopers Endowment; acquired by IBM 2002) funding third-party practitioner-focused research on public management at federal, state, and local levels. Publishes 25+ reports per year on digital modernization, AI adoption, workforce, procurement, and service delivery. 2024-25 publications include GenAI for state government, AI-powered procurement, federal workforce transformation, and reducing administrative burden. Hosts forums, radio program, and maintains practitioner fellows. Led by Executive Director Dan Chenok (former career federal CIO executive).

name: Information Technology and Innovation Foundation (ITIF)
description: Nonpartisan science and tech policy think tank. Research on government IT modernization, AI policy, and digital infrastructure. Published 'After DOGE: Trump's Chance to Modernize.'

name: Institute for Progress (IFP)
description: The Institute for Progress (IFP) is a nonpartisan think tank founded 2022 focused on innovation policy: metascience, immigration, emerging technology, and AI infrastructure. Provides technical assistance to federal agencies and runs Capitol Hill briefings for congressional staff. Produces rapid-turnaround policy analysis on high-stakes technology and science policy questions.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures, Sloan Foundation, Schmidt Futures, Open Philanthropy, Astera Foundation

name: Jain Family Institute
description: Nonpartisan applied research organization founded 2014. Active work on guaranteed income program design (advised Compton Pledge, Stockton SEED, federal Child Tax Credit), digital ethics and AI governance, and macroeconomic policy for government. Advises city programs, state legislatures, and federal policymakers. Bridges academic research and government implementation.
funding_detail: Private foundation funding (Bobby Jain); Open Society Foundations

name: J-PAL North America
description: MIT-based research center running randomized evaluations in partnership with state and local governments. State and Local Innovation Initiative embeds affiliated researchers with government agencies to generate rigorous evidence across housing, criminal justice, workforce, health, and education. LEVER Evaluation Incubator (co-run with Results for America) provides government agencies with technical assistance and research connections. Twice-annual RFP cycles fund government-partnered evaluations. 1,100+ affiliated researchers at universities worldwide. Has partnered with 18+ US state and local governments since 2015.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures, Gates Foundation, JPB Foundation, federal research grants

name: Manhattan Institute
description: Center-right think tank focused on urban policy and public-sector reform. Governance program promotes transparency, accountability, and evidence-based reforms. Published 'Digital Transformation: Wiring the Responsive City.' City Journal magazine covers urban governance and innovation. Cities Director John Ketcham leads governance work.
funding_detail: Conservative philanthropic base; individual and foundation donors

name: MDRC
description: MDRC (Manpower Demonstration Research Corporation) is a nonprofit research organization founded 1974, the gold standard for rigorous randomized controlled trial evaluation of social and education programs. Works directly with government agencies on program design and evaluation. Key node for evidence-based policy, outcomes measurement, and social program evaluation problem statements. Arnold Ventures multi-year strategic partner.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures (multi-year); Annie E. Casey, Rockefeller; government agency contracts

name: Mercatus Center (George Mason University)
description: University-based research center. Regulatory reform, permitting modernization, and government process improvement research. Published influential work on regulatory accumulation and its effects on government capacity. Technology policy program.
funding_detail: George Mason University + Koch-affiliated and broad donor base

name: MIT GOV/LAB
description: Research lab studying government innovation, political accountability, and institutional design using field experiments and design thinking.

name: National Association of Counties (NACo)
description: The only national organization representing all 3,069 US county governments. Runs the County Tech Xchange peer network for county CIOs, published the AI County Compass governance guide (2024), and hosts regional AI forums. Complementary to NLC which covers municipalities; NACo covers the county layer of government.

name: National Civic League
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit (est. 1894) promoting civic engagement and government innovation. All-America City Award (oldest community recognition in US). Research on collaborative governance, civic infrastructure, and democratic innovation.

name: National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL)
description: Bipartisan organization serving all 7,500+ state legislators and legislative staff across all 50 states, commonwealths, and territories. Produces nonpartisan policy research, technical assistance, and legislative tracking across every major issue area including technology, AI (tracked 450+ bills in 23 AI categories in 2024), cybersecurity, broadband, and digital government. Annual Legislative Summit and Fall Forum. Budget of ~$40M. Dual headquarters in Denver and DC.
funding_detail: State legislative appropriations (member dues) + federal grants + foundation grants

name: National League of Cities (NLC)
description: Membership organization and research body representing 19,000+ cities, towns, and villages - serving 90%+ of Americans. Annual State of Cities report (12th edition 2025) surveys mayors on top priorities. Publishes State and Local Fiscal Facts and digital government research. Partners with Beeck Center on digital services guidance for local governments. Hosts annual City Summit and State of GovTech conference (with CivStart) for city CIOs and elected officials. Advocates for federal policy supporting city capacity, broadband, and AI governance.
funding_detail: City membership dues + foundation grants + federal grants

name: New America: Public Interest Technology
description: PIT program: fellowships, The Commons (procurement research), policy research. Co-convenes PIT University Network (PIT-UN): 63 institutions, $16M+ deployed.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: NGA Center for Best Practices
description: The only R&D organization in the nation that directly serves governors. Develops innovative policy solutions through five divisions (economic/workforce, education, environment/energy/transportation, health, homeland security). Runs policy academies with cohorts of state teams on specific implementation challenges (SNAP E&T delivery, healthcare workforce, service-to-career pathways). Publishes 50-state analyses and provides direct TA to governors' offices. Annual budget ~$30M. Funded by state dues and federal grants.
funding_detail: State appropriations (population-based dues) + federal grants + foundation support

name: Niskanen Center: Project on State Capacity
description: Dedicated state capacity research initiative. Published 'The How We Need Now' capacity agenda. Policy research on civil service reform, digital modernization, product operating model, implementation-focused legislation.

name: Pew Charitable Trusts: Government Performance
description: Nonpartisan research organization with a dedicated Strengthen State Government program producing the definitive empirical research on state fiscal health, rainy day funds, tax policy, and government performance. Fiscal 50 platform tracks all 50 states on revenue, spending, and reserves. Also tracks state courts modernization and government accountability. Explicitly nonadvocacy - research is designed to inform rather than persuade policymakers.
funding_detail: $7B+ endowment; earned revenue from research contracts

name: Progressive Policy Institute (PPI)
description: Center-left think tank (Third Way/New Democrat tradition). Technology and innovation policy program. Research on government digital transformation, broadband, AI policy, and building state capacity through technology. Founded by Democratic Leadership Council veterans.

name: R Street Institute
description: Free-market think tank producing research on limited, effective government, regulatory reform, and tech policy.

name: RAND Corporation
description: Nonpartisan research institute. Center on AI, Security & Technology (RAND CAST) researches transformative AI policy. Published work on scaling AI in state/local government, adaptive governance frameworks, and national AI strategy. Founding partner of PIT University Network. Also does direct government consulting.
funding_detail: Open Philanthropy, government contracts, endowment, broad donor base

name: RegLab (Stanford)
description: The Regulation, Evaluation, and Governance Lab (RegLab) at Stanford University partners directly with government agencies to design, implement, and evaluate AI and data science solutions for core governance functions. Agency partners include IRS, EPA, DOL, and Santa Clara County. IRS audit disparity analysis is landmark work. Senate testimony on AI in government shaped the Biden AI Executive Order and OMB memorandum. Runs talent pipeline programs into public sector.
funding_detail: Stanford Impact Labs (3.5M, 4-year); government agency partnerships

name: Responsible AI Institute (RAI Institute)
description: Independent nonprofit providing AI certification, conformity assessments, and responsible AI tools for government agencies. Develops standards and frameworks for trustworthy AI procurement and deployment.

name: Roosevelt Institute
description: Left-of-center think tank focused on economic policy and government capacity research. Primary output is policy research on public investment, industrial policy, and government effectiveness. Student network is a separate affiliated entity.

name: Searchlight Institute
description: A Democratic-aligned policy think tank focused on reshaping the party's strategy toward broader, more electorally viable positions.

name: Stanford Digital Economy Lab
description: Research on technology's impact on economy, work, and institutions (Erik Brynjolfsson). Quantitative research on AI economics and labor markets.

name: Stanford HAI (Human-Centered AI Institute)
description: The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI) studies AI's social, ethical, and governance implications. Publishes the annual AI Index report, the authoritative global benchmark for AI progress. Runs AI policy fellowship programs placing researchers with government agencies. Active engagement with Congress, OMB, and federal AI policy development.
funding_detail: Stanford University; HAI industry partners; foundation grants

name: The GovLab (NYU Tandon + Burnes Center at Northeastern)
description: Research lab studying how technology and data improve governance. Open data, data collaboratives, collective intelligence, and citizen engagement.

name: Urban Institute
description: Nonpartisan research organization studying social and economic policy. Research on government finance, social safety net delivery, benefits modernization, and evidence-based policy implementation. Data tools and interactive dashboards for policymakers. Work on how government systems deliver (or fail to deliver) services.
funding_detail: Foundation grants + government research contracts + endowment

name: Volcker Alliance
description: Research and ratings on government effectiveness, public finance, and government workforce. Government-to-University Initiative for MPA/MPP pipeline.

name: Yale Tobin Center for Economic Policy
description: Domestic policy center providing direct technical assistance to governments and multi-university research partnerships on evidence-based policy.

name: We the Doers
description: A nonpartisan organization of former senior federal career civil servants producing practical reform recommendations for agency leaders, the executive branch, and Congress. Founded December 2025. Focused on removing structural barriers to effective service delivery.
funding_detail: No public funding disclosure as of June 2026.

name: ClearGov
description: Cloud budget cycle management software for local governments and school districts. Platform covers capital, personnel, and operating budgets with collaboration workflows, digital budget books, and financial reporting. Serves 2,000+ customers managing over $540 billion in budgets.
funding_detail: $34.5M total raised; Series B (2024) led by Frontier Growth; prior investors include Kepha Partners and MassVentures

name: DebtBook
description: Treasury management platform purpose-built for government and nonprofit finance teams. Automates GASB 87/96 compliance, ACFR note generation, debt tracking, and cash positioning in a single system. Used by 40% of the 250 largest U.S. municipalities and counties; 2,100+ customers nationwide.
funding_detail: Privately held; no publicly disclosed external funding; legal entity is Fifth Asset Inc.

name: BondLink
description: Cloud investor relations and debt management platform for municipal bond issuers. Enables state and local governments to communicate directly with investors, manage disclosure compliance, and execute bond sales. Clients include State of California, City of Chicago, and University of Texas. $34.1M raised.
funding_detail: $34.1M total raised across 4 rounds; Series B (2021); investors include Intercontinental Exchange and Franklin Templeton

name: Hazel
description: AI-powered procurement software for government agencies. Automates solicitation drafting, vendor matching, compliance checks, and proposal evaluation; procurement officers retain all final decisions. Contracts span school districts through the U.S. Navy. YC W2024; seed stage.
funding_detail: Y Combinator (W2024); seed stage; total undisclosed

name: Cardinality.ai
description: Pre-built AI SaaS platform for Health and Human Services agencies covering child welfare, child support, SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, and workforce development. Low-code architecture enables agencies to modernize up to 50% faster than custom builds. Serves 5 states across 11 agencies; solutions reach 23M+ constituents. $26M raised.
funding_detail: $26M raised across multiple rounds; Series B (April 2023) led by Boathouse Capital; prior investors include Attain Capital and BarronKent

name: Govstream.ai
description: AI copilot for permit technicians, planners, and reviewers. Sits atop existing permitting systems to answer staff questions, validate submitted documents, and pre-check applications against municipal codes before formal review. Live in Bellevue WA (30% reduction in routine inquiries) and Louisville KY. $4.9M raised.
funding_detail: $4.9M total; $3.6M Seed (Dec 2025) led by 47th Street Partners; pre-seed from Nellore Capital and Ascend

name: Just Appraised
description: AI workflow software for county property tax assessors and clerks. Automates deed processing, ownership transfers, exemption management, and taxpayer communication. Serves 300+ counties across 30 states. Stanford Business School origin; YC-backed.
funding_detail: Y Combinator-backed; seed stage; total undisclosed

name: Forerunner
description: AI-powered geospatial platform for government built-environment operations. Unifies floodplain compliance, code enforcement, permitting, infrastructure asset tracking, and grant management in one system with mobile field tools and automated reporting. Trusted by 190+ communities across 26 states including CA Dept. of Water Resources and FL Division of Emergency Management. $39M raised.
funding_detail: $39M total; $26.3M Series B (Feb 2026) led by Wellington Management; prior investors include Gutter Capital

name: Deckard Technologies
description: AI platform for short-term and long-term rental compliance. Scans 15M+ listings across 10,000+ rental websites daily to identify unregistered properties, automate permit tracking, collect occupancy taxes, and streamline enforcement. Used by 400+ jurisdictions in the U.S., Canada, and Australia; average client STR compliance rate of 95%. $3.5M raised.

name: Aclima
description: Block-by-block air quality and greenhouse gas measurement platform for government environmental agencies. Deploys vehicle-mounted sensor networks to map pollution at 100,000x greater resolution than traditional monitoring stations. Holds a $27M contract with California Air Resources Board; partners include NY State DEC and EPA. Public Benefit Corporation; $64M raised.
funding_detail: $64M total; $40M Series B (2020); $13M additional round (Sept 2024); investors include Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, Bosch Ventures, and Kapor Capital

name: Automotus
description: Computer vision platform for automated curb management. Cellular-enabled cameras monitor loading zones and curbside activity, automate commercial vehicle payments, enforce violations, and provide real-time analytics for city planners. Deployed in dozens of U.S. markets. $26M raised.
funding_detail: $26M total; $9M equity round (Dec 2025) led by Santa Barbara Venture Partners and Weatherford Capital; $9M seed (2022) led by CityRock Venture Partners

name: DeepWalk
description: iPhone LiDAR-based software for municipalities to assess sidewalk systems for ADA compliance. Staff scan with a mobile app; the platform generates 3D models, compliance reports, and construction documents needed for ADA transition plans. Serves cities, counties, and universities across the U.S. $1.8M raised.

name: Ontra Mobility
description: AI transit planning and dispatch platform for cities and agencies, built by former Google engineers with PhDs in operations research. Forecasts demand, optimizes fixed-route networks, integrates on-demand zones, and dispatches in real time; powered MARTA Reach (Atlanta) and CAT SMART (Savannah). YC S24; selected for 2026 Transit Tech Lab proof of concept with MTA NYCT and LIRR.

name: Waypoint Transit
description: AI city planner that generates civil infrastructure studies and transportation planning reports for municipalities and transit agencies. Automates GIS analysis, data collection, and report generation to reduce planning timelines from years to months at 30% of traditional consultant cost. Live in 10+ municipalities including Duluth MN and MN DOT. YC W25; $500K raised.

name: Waterly
description: Data management and regulatory compliance software for water and wastewater utilities. Replaces spreadsheets and clipboards with real-time operational data entry, chemical dosage calculation, regulatory report generation, and SCADA integration. Designed by water operators; serves rural communities through large cities. $4M raised.
funding_detail: $4M raised; Series A (Aug 2025) led by Burnt Island Ventures; prior investors include Emerald Technology Ventures and CivStart

name: Mark43
description: Cloud records management system and computer-aided dispatch for law enforcement. Replaces legacy on-premise infrastructure with a CJIS-compliant integrated platform for incident tracking, reporting, evidence management, and inter-agency data sharing. Deployed by DOI across 6 law enforcement programs covering 3,000 officers and 850+ locations nationwide.
funding_detail: Multiple rounds; $27M Series B led by General Catalyst and Spark Capital; investors include Goldman Sachs and Jeff Bezos; total undisclosed

name: CivicEye
description: Cloud software for law enforcement, prosecutors, and courts on a unified platform. Covers records management (CivicRMS), digital evidence (CivicDocs), and case management (CivicCase). Adopted statewide by the Tennessee District Attorney General Conference; 150+ agencies nationwide. $12.4M raised.
funding_detail: $12.4M Series A (July 2022) led by Cercano Management; participation from Relevance Ventures

name: Ordinal
description: AI research assistant for local government staff. Uses retrieval-augmented generation against approved internal documents -- municipal codes, ordinances, GIS data, and meeting minutes -- to provide fast, source-cited answers without training on external data. Live in cities across Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, and California. $1M raised.
funding_detail: $1M Seed (Aug 2025) led by Plains Ventures; participation from Winrock International and The Venture Center Arkansas Fund

name: GovGuard
description: AI agents for government FOIA and public records workflows. Automatically searches archived records, flags sensitive information for redaction, and drafts response letters for staff review; clerks retain full legal review authority over all disclosures. YC-backed; seed stage.
funding_detail: Y Combinator-backed; seed stage; total undisclosed

name: RapidSOS
description: Public safety AI platform connecting 600M+ devices and sensors to 22,000+ emergency agencies in real time. Gives 911 dispatchers location data, medical profiles, and contextual intelligence from connected devices and cameras via its HARMONY AI system. Has supported over one billion emergencies. $450M+ raised; $1B valuation as of November 2025.
funding_detail: $450M+ raised across multiple rounds; $100M round (Nov 2025) led by Apax Digital at $1B valuation; prior investors include Highland Capital Partners, Insight Partners, BlackRock, and NightDragon

name: Swiftly
description: Real-time transit data platform for transit agencies. Provides operational analytics, on-time performance monitoring, schedule optimization, and real-time passenger information. Works with nearly half of the top 50 U.S. transit agencies including MBTA, LA Metro, SEPTA, and MDOT MTA. 2025 strategic investment from Cove Hill Partners with JMI Equity participation.
funding_detail: $200M+ raised across multiple rounds; 2025 strategic investment led by Cove Hill Partners with JMI Equity; prior investors include Renewal Funds, Ford Smart Mobility, and Samsung NEXT

name: The Callimachus Project
description: Nonprofit using AI to capture institutional knowledge from departing federal civil servants. Conducts long-form interviews with former employees, then summarizes, stores, and analyzes the knowledge to build a free, searchable AI chatbot database intended for Hill staff and transition teams working to rebuild civil service capacity.
funding_detail: Private philanthropy via fiscal sponsor has funded founding and early proof of concept; seeking further philanthropic funding to build out AI interview-collection process and chatbot database/interface.
